title: Recommender Baselines & Problem Formulation
interviewAnswer: Start with popularity, recency and simple content/history baselines. Define whether the task is rating prediction, top-N ranking, next-item prediction or candidate generation because metrics and data construction differ.
keyPoints: Negative samples are usually unobserved, not true dislikes.
Temporal splits better reflect recommendation deployment.
why: Recommender Baselines & Problem Formulation appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Start with popularity, recency and simple content/history baselines. Define whether the task is rating prediction, top-N ranking, next-item prediction or candidate generation because metrics and data construction differ. Negative samples are usually unobserved, not true dislikes. Temporal splits better reflect recommendation deployment. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Compare a personalized model with most-popular-by-category and recently-popular baselines.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Recommender Baselines & Problem Formulation make?
How would you validate or debug Recommender Baselines & Problem Formulation in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
